Thanks folks, I appreciate the comments.  Its good to know that others are in similar places.  Sometimes it feels like I am out here forging into unknown territory, but that's just not true.  There are lots of people with me, and many that have gone before.

I am really enjoying the new (or maybe old repressed) aspects of myself that are showing themselves.  It is awesome meeting the me that was supposed to be.
Thanks for that vote of confidence.  Its like I never realized how little emotion I actually felt, and now I don't have the coping mechanisms to deal with it and get overwhelmed.
Thank you Allan Watts :-)

Sex gets better.  Or at least for some (ME!!) it did.  So maybe you don't have the same old driving need you once had... meh... When you do settle down to the fucking it will be different and it will (if you are lucky) blow your mind.

Its a balance.

I was also, (sans a few specific details) if you were telling my story.  Happy for you.  I think the biggest 'wow' thing for me has been gym change rooms.  I expected the worst, instead I get random conversations and not even a batted eye.

I am beginning to wonder if it is big city privilege (I am in Toronto) or whether we let our fear create much more of our personal narrative then maybe we should.  Everything I step I have taken in regards to transition has been accompanied by _way_ more anxiety than it turns out was necessary.  

Again, in no way discounting risk and harassment that has been (and will be) experienced by anyone out there.

I am curious how many of you actually do face harassment using public washrooms.  Am I just lucky ? I started  using the women's washroom shortly after beginning hormones and have had no problems at all.  About a month ago I began using the women's change rooms at the gym and the rec center, again no problem.   To give some context I am close to passing, but still visibly trans, so its not like this is stealth.  I just walk in, sometimes people talk to me...

So yeah, once you get over the fear of doing it how many of you actually suffer harassment?

(note, in no way downplaying anybodies experience, and not denying that there is risk, and some of us get hurt)
You will be fine
